Compare active and passive acquired immunity.

contentBlocks.text: Methods of the body's resistance to disease

rows: Cellular components: B and T lymphocytes

contentBlocks.text: Types of acquired immunity
Active acquired immunity

The book explains that exposure to an antigen leads the immune system to produce antibodies and form memory cells. Examples given include immunization with live attenuated or dead microbes and toxoids.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: المناعة النشطة تحدث عند تعرض الجهاز المناعي لمستضد فينتج أجسامًا مضادة وتتكون خلايا ذاكرة. ومن أمثلة الكتاب التحصين بميكروبات حية مضعفة أو ميتة أو بالذوفان.
Passive acquired immunity
A person receives ready-made antibodies or immune cells from another person. The textbook gives receiving immunoglobulin as an example.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: المناعة السلبية تحدث عند الحصول على أجسام مضادة جاهزة أو خلايا مناعية من شخص آخر؛ ومثال الكتاب إعطاء Immunoglobulin.

rows: The person's immune system responds to an antigen

lessons.title: Chest Pain — Angina Pectoris
objectives: Explain the topic using the supplied textbook.
Identify manifestations, investigations and complications described in the source.
Review key terminology and nursing-care themes in the chapter.

contentBlocks.text: Textbook-based explanation

The book defines angina pectoris as severe pain beneath the sternum, described as squeezing, pressing or burning. It links it to narrowing of coronary arteries (atherosclerosis). Listed associated factors include obesity, diabetes, elevated triglycerides and cholesterol, hypertension, heredity, frequent animal-fat intake, smoking and lack of physical activity. Pain may increase with exercise, eating or severe cold, may also occur at rest, and can spread to the arm, wrist, shoulder or teeth. Sweating and nausea may accompany it. The textbook lists resting or stress ECG, nuclear scan and cardiac catheterization as diagnostic methods.

contentBlocks.title: شرح بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: الذبحة الصدرية ألم شديد أسفل عظمة القص يوصف بالعصر أو الضغط أو الحرقان، ويربطه الكتاب بضيق الشرايين التاجية نتيجة التصلب. يذكر عوامل مثل السمنة والسكري وارتفاع الدهون وضغط الدم والتدخين وقلة النشاط. وقد يزيد الألم مع المجهود أو الطعام أو البرد، وقد يمتد للذراع أو الكتف أو الأسنان، مع عرق وغثيان.
Comparison / revision table

rows: Severe squeezing, pressing or burning pain beneath sternum
Obesity, diabetes, high lipids, hypertension, heredity, animal fats, smoking, inactivity
ECG, stress ECG, nuclear scan, cardiac catheterization

lessons.title: Ischemic Heart Disease — Myocardial Infarction
objectives: Explain the topic using the supplied textbook.
Identify manifestations, investigations and complications described in the source.
Review key terminology and nursing-care themes in the chapter.

contentBlocks.text: Textbook-based explanation

The textbook describes myocardial infarction as severe chest pain resembling angina but longer and more intense, with profuse sweating, nausea and severe fear. It attributes it to complete coronary-artery blockage causing death of part of the heart muscle. Listed features include pain beneath the sternum spreading to the left arm, shoulder and neck, sometimes a burning stomach sensation, vomiting and cold extremities. The chapter lists heart failure, pulmonary edema and arrhythmias among complications, and names ECG, cardiac enzymes, CBC/ESR, chest X-ray and echocardiography as investigations.

contentBlocks.title: شرح بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: يصف الكتاب احتشاء عضلة القلب بأنه ألم يشبه الذبحة لكنه أطول وأشد، وقد يصاحبه عرق شديد وغثيان وخوف. ويربطه بانسداد كامل في الشريان التاجي يؤدي إلى موت جزء من عضلة القلب. ومن المظاهر امتداد الألم للذراع الأيسر والكتف والرقبة، وقد يصاحبه قيء وبرودة الأطراف.

contentBlocks.text: Core explanation | الشرح الأساسي

The book defines hypertension as blood pressure of 140/90 or above on three different readings. It distinguishes primary hypertension from secondary forms associated with kidney, thyroid, adrenal, brain disorders or some medicines. Many cases have no specific symptoms.

contentBlocks.title: الخلاصة بالعربي | Key point

contentBlocks.text: Core explanation | الشرح الأساسي

Asthma is described as recurrent breathing difficulty caused by bronchial narrowing and viscous secretions. Triggers listed include dust, feathers, animals, fungi, pollen, fumes, some foods and medicines, and exercise in children. Features include chest tightness, dyspnea, wheezing and cough.

lessons.title: Gastrointestinal Bleeding
objectives: Explain the topic using the supplied textbook.
Identify manifestations, investigations and complications described in the source.
Review key terminology and nursing-care themes in the chapter.

contentBlocks.text: Textbook-based explanation

The textbook divides causes into upper-GI sources (esophagitis, esophageal varices or cancer, gastritis, gastric ulcer or cancer, duodenitis and duodenal ulcer) and lower-GI sources (colitis, ulcerative colitis, angiodysplasia, hemorrhoids, colon polyps, diverticulitis, ischemic colitis and colon cancer). It describes hematemesis, melena and hematochezia. Assessment includes vital signs and tests such as CBC, blood group and crossmatch, kidney and liver function, prothrombin time and electrolytes. The source outlines volume replacement and treatment of the cause.

contentBlocks.title: شرح بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: يقسم الكتاب أسباب النزيف إلى علوي وسفلي. ويعرض ثلاث صور: القيء الدموي Hematemesis، والبراز الأسود Melena، والنزيف الشرجي Hematochezia. ويشمل التقييم العلامات الحيوية وتحاليل الدم ووظائف الكلى والكبد والتجلط والأملاح، ثم تعويض الدم والسوائل وعلاج السبب.
Comparison / revision table

rows: Vomiting blood or coffee-ground material; usually upper GI source
Black tarry stool; upper GI, small intestine or proximal colon source
Rectal bleeding; usually lower GI, sometimes severe upper GI bleeding
